title: Messages
description: Workers message each other by callsign across runtimes: the tower carries what Claude Code's own SendMessage can't, to or from a worker on opencode, into the receiver's inbox, signed with the sender's callsign.

sent.description: The worker sent a message through the tower: the receiver's session, and the text as written, before the envelope that signs it.

to.description: The worker's callsign, looked for on the sender's floor, then on every floor.

text.description: The message: the receiver has none of your context.

send.description: Hand a message to a worker's inbox, signed with the calling worker's callsign: its runtime takes it in as a prompt once it is free. For a pair Claude Code's own SendMessage can't connect: a worker on opencode at either end.

guidance.brief: Workers on opencode are messaged too: SendMessage to their callsign, carried by the tower. A <tower-message from="CALLSIGN"> prompt is that worker's message.
guidance.full:
The tower carries messages between workers that Claude Code's own SendMessage can't connect: a worker on opencode, at either end.

- On Claude Code: SendMessage as always. `to` set to a worker's callsign reaches it whatever it runs on: what Claude can't deliver itself, to a worker on opencode, goes through the tower.
- On opencode: the SendMessage tool, `{to, message}`, `to` the callsign.
- From a shell: `tower x messages send <CALLSIGN> <<'EOF'` … `EOF`.

A message waits in the receiver's inbox until it is free, and reaches it as a prompt `<tower-message from="CALLSIGN">…</tower-message>`: that worker's message, not the user's. Answer it the same way, to that callsign. Two workers both on Claude Code message each other with SendMessage alone; the tower refuses to carry theirs. A worker that started before this was on its floor has no inbox: `tower submit` types into its composer instead.
